title: Summum Bonum
author: Robert Fludd
query: Summum bonum magiae cabalae alchymiae fratrum Roseae Crucis
epithet: Fludd's defence of the Rose Cross and its magic
summary: Fludd's reply to Mersenne under a pseudonym, defending magic, cabala and alchemy and the Brotherhood of the Rose Cross — the source of the famous rose-and-cross engraving 'Dat Rosa Mel Apibus'.

title: Medicina Catholica
author: Robert Fludd
query: Medicina catholica Fludd Frankfurt
epithet: A weather-glass of the winds and the body
summary: Fludd's macrocosm-microcosm medicine, in which the health of the body answers to the winds, stars and archangels of the greater world — his fullest picture of man mirrored in the cosmos.

title: The Three Principles of the Divine Essence
author: Jacob Böhme
query: Concerning the Three Principles of the Divine Essence Behmen
epithet: The three worlds within God and man
summary: Böhme's account of the three principles — the dark fire-world, the light love-world and this outer world — the metaphysics of the divine self-generation that underlies all his later books, in Sparrow's English.

title: The High and Deep Searching Out of the Threefold Life of Man
author: Jacob Böhme
query: Threefold Life of Man Boehme Sparrow
epithet: Man's life in the three worlds at once
summary: Böhme's meditation on the threefold life of man — according to the outer world, the dark and the divine — one of the central works of the shoemaker-theosophist, in the Ellistone/Sparrow translation.

title: The Way to Christ
author: Jacob Böhme
query: The Way to Christ Discovered Jacob Behmen
epithet: The only book Böhme published in his life
summary: The nine devotional treatises on repentance, resignation and the new birth that were the one work of Böhme's printed before he died — the practical, mystical core of his theosophy.

title: Forty Questions of the Soul
author: Jacob Böhme
query: Forty Questions of the Soul Boehme
epithet: The origin, nature and end of the soul
summary: Böhme's answers to forty questions on the soul put to him by Balthasar Walther, with the famous 'Philosophic Globe' diagram of the soul's turning between the dark and light worlds.

title: Theologia Mystica
author: John Pordage
query: Theologia Mystica Pordage
epithet: The English Behmenist's map of the invisible worlds
summary: Pordage's posthumous account of the 'eternal invisibles' and the angelical world — the fullest statement of the English Behmenist theosophy that gathered around him and Jane Lead.

title: A Fountain of Gardens
author: Jane Lead
query: A Fountain of Gardens Jane Lead
epithet: The visionary diary of the Philadelphian prophetess
summary: Lead's vast spiritual journal of visions of the Virgin Sophia — the record of the revelations that guided the Philadelphian Society and carried Böhme's theosophy into a prophetic, female voice.

title: The Revelation of Revelations
author: Jane Lead
query: The Revelation of Revelations Jane Lead
epithet: An opening of the sealed book of Wisdom
summary: Lead's early vision of the Wonders of God's Creation and the manifestation of the Virgin Wisdom — the book that announced the Sophianic mysticism at the heart of the Philadelphian movement.

title: Lumen de Lumine
author: Thomas Vaughan
query: Lumen de Lumine Vaughan Eugenius Philalethes
epithet: A new magical light, guided by Thalia
summary: Vaughan's Hermetic treatise on the light hidden in nature, framed as a vision led by the nymph Thalia — the alchemical mysticism of the man who Englished the Rosicrucian manifestos.

title: Magia Adamica
author: Thomas Vaughan
query: Magia Adamica Vaughan Eugenius Philalethes
epithet: The antiquity of magic, from Adam down
summary: Vaughan's defence of magic as the true wisdom taught to Adam and handed down through the ancients — a spirited apology for the art, appended with the Rosicrucian 'Coelum Terrae'.
imprint: London: T. W. for H. Blunden, 1650

title: The Holy Guide
author: John Heydon
query: The Holy Guide John Heydon Rosie Crucian
epithet: The self-styled Rosicrucian's guide to all wisdom
summary: Heydon's sprawling compendium of 'Rosie Crucian' physic, prophecy and magic — much of it lifted from Bacon and Agrippa — the book that did most to fix the popular English image of the Rosicrucian adept.

title: Themis Aurea: The Laws of the Fraternity of the Rosie Crosse
author: Michael Maier
query: Themis Aurea Laws Fraternity Rosie Crosse
epithet: The golden laws of the Rose Cross brotherhood
summary: Maier's discourse on the laws and customs of the Rosicrucian fraternity, Englished for the Interregnum reader — one of the fullest early defences of the order's existence and aims.

title: Divine Love and Wisdom
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: Angelic Wisdom Divine Love Wisdom Swedenborg
epithet: The metaphysics of the two that make the world
summary: Swedenborg's account of the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom as the two constituents of God and of all creation, with his doctrine of degrees and correspondences — the philosophical spine of his theology.

title: The True Christian Religion
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: True Christian Religion Swedenborg
epithet: Swedenborg's whole theology in one volume
summary: The last and largest work Swedenborg published, the complete system of the New Church — the universal theology he offered as the Second Coming realised in doctrine rather than in a returning man.

title: The Apocalypse Revealed
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: Apocalypse Revealed Swedenborg
epithet: The Book of Revelation opened by correspondences
summary: Swedenborg's verse-by-verse reading of the Apocalypse as a description of the states of the church and the spiritual world, decoded through his science of correspondences.

title: Conjugial Love
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: Conjugial Love Swedenborg Delights of Wisdom
epithet: Marriage as it endures into heaven
summary: Swedenborg's treatise on the 'delights of wisdom concerning conjugial love' — his teaching that true marriage is a spiritual union that continues among the angels, with reports of the heavens he claimed to have seen.

title: L'Homme de désir
author: Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin
query: Homme de desir Saint-Martin
epithet: The unknown philosopher's song of the fallen soul
summary: Saint-Martin's lyrical meditations on the desire that draws the fallen human being back toward its divine source — the devotional heart of the Martinist path he taught after breaking with ceremonial magic.

title: The Immortality of the Soul
author: Henry More
query: Immortality of the Soul Henry More
epithet: The Cambridge Platonist's proof of the spirit-world
summary: More's demonstration of the soul's immortality and of a graded world of spirits and 'spissitude' — the Cambridge Platonist metaphysics that gave later psychical research its philosophical warrant.

title: Der güldene Griff
author: Valentin Weigel
query: Der guldene Griff Weigel Gnothi Seauton
epithet: The golden handle: all knowing is self-knowing
summary: Weigel's treatise arguing that all knowledge arises from within the knower — a mystical epistemology that fed directly into Böhme and the German theosophical stream.

title: Das Geheimnis der göttlichen Sophia
author: Gottfried Arnold
query: Geheimniss der goettlichen Sophia Arnold
epithet: The mystery of the divine Wisdom
summary: Arnold's treatise on the divine Sophia, the heavenly Wisdom of Böhme and the Philadelphians — the scholarly Pietist's gathering of the whole Sophia tradition into one book.

title: L'Économie divine
author: Pierre Poiret
query: Oeconomie divine Poiret
epithet: A whole system of mystical divinity
summary: Poiret's seven-volume system of divine economy — the philosophical Cartesian-turned-mystic who edited Antoinette Bourignon and gathered the quietist and theosophic currents of his century.

title: The Spirit of Prayer
author: William Law
query: Spirit of Prayer William Law
epithet: Böhme Englished by a master of prose
summary: Law's dialogues on the birth of God in the soul, the fruit of his late immersion in Böhme — the most eloquent English statement of the theosophical mysticism he spent his last years expounding.

title: Via Lucis
author: Jan Amos Comenius
query: Via lucis Comenius
epithet: The way of light: a pansophic college of nations
summary: Comenius's plan for the universal spread of light through a pansophic college, a universal language and a reformed learning — the eirenic, Rosicrucian-tinged utopia of the great educator.

title: La Lumière du Monde
author: Antoinette Bourignon
query: Lumiere du monde Bourignon
epithet: The visionary who gathered her own disciples
summary: Bourignon's account of her inner light and revelations — the Flemish mystic whose claim to a direct divine illumination drew a following across Protestant Europe and scandalised its churches.

title: The Worship and Love of God
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: Worship and Love of God Swedenborg
epithet: A prose poem of creation on the eve of the visions
summary: Swedenborg's rhapsodic Latin account of the creation of the world and of Adam and Eve — the last work of his scientific period, written as his inner sight was opening.

title: Earths in the Universe
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: Earths in the Universe Swedenborg
epithet: The spirits of the other planets
summary: Swedenborg's report of his conversations with the spirits of the moon and the planets — the strangest of his shorter works, and a favourite of the later occult and science-fiction imagination.

title: Aurora, or the Day-Spring
author: Jacob Böhme
query: Aurora Day-Spring Behmen Sparrow
epithet: The first, unfinished dawn of Böhme's vision
summary: Böhme's first book, the ecstatic and unfinished Aurora, in John Sparrow's English — the work whose seizure by the church first made the shoemaker of Görlitz notorious.

title: Signatura Rerum, or the Signature of All Things
author: Jacob Böhme
query: Signatura Rerum Signature of All Things Behmen
epithet: How each thing bears the sign of its nature
summary: Böhme's doctrine that every created thing carries an outward signature disclosing its inward quality — the book that gave the doctrine of signatures its most influential mystical statement, in English.

title: The Way to Divine Knowledge
author: William Law
query: Way to Divine Knowledge William Law
epithet: Law's dialogues opening the way to Böhme
summary: Law's dialogues meant to prepare the reader for the deep writings of Böhme — the theosophical capstone of the great English devotional writer's later years.
imprint: London: W. Innys and J. Richardson, 1752

title: Mosaicall Philosophy
author: Robert Fludd
query: Mosaicall Philosophy Fludd
epithet: Fludd's Genesis cosmology, in English at last
summary: The English version of Fludd's Philosophia Moysaica, grounding the whole frame of nature in the light and darkness of the first day — his system made available to the English reader.

title: The Labyrinth of the World and the Paradise of the Heart
author: Jan Amos Comenius
query: Labyrinth of the World and Paradise of the Heart Comenius
epithet: A pilgrim's disillusioned tour of the world
summary: Comenius's allegory of a pilgrim wandering the vain and cheating city of the world until he finds rest in the paradise of the heart — the Czech classic of the great pansophic reformer.

title: Anthroposophia Theomagica
author: Thomas Vaughan
query: Anthroposophia Theomagica Vaughan Eugenius Philalethes
epithet: A discourse of the nature of man and his state after death
summary: Vaughan's first Hermetic treatise on the nature of man, the soul and the world-spirit — the book that drew Henry More into a famous pamphlet war with the Welsh alchemist.
imprint: London: T. W. for H. Blunden, 1650

title: Mundorum Explicatio
author: Samuel Pordage
query: Mundorum Explicatio Pordage
epithet: The Behmenist cosmos rendered in verse
summary: A long allegorical poem of the several worlds and the soul's regeneration, from the circle of John Pordage — the English Behmenist vision turned into epic verse.

title: The Intercourse between the Soul and the Body
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
query: Intercourse between the Soul and the Body Swedenborg
epithet: How spirit and flesh are joined
summary: Swedenborg's short treatise on the relation of soul and body, resolving the old problem through his doctrine of influx — a compact statement of the metaphysics behind his visions.

title: Jacob Behmen's Theosophick Philosophy Unfolded
author: Edward Taylor
query: Jacob Behmen Theosophick Philosophy Unfolded Taylor
epithet: An early English key to Böhme
summary: Edward Taylor's exposition and defence of Böhme's theosophy for the English reader — one of the earliest attempts to make the difficult German mystic systematic and accessible.

title: The Tree of Faith
author: Jane Lead
query: The Tree of Faith Jane Lead
epithet: The growing tree of the regenerate soul
summary: Lead's treatise on the tree of faith planted and growing in the believing soul — one of the visionary tracts of the Philadelphian prophetess and her Sophianic mysticism.

title: The Vanity of Dogmatizing
author: Joseph Glanvill
query: The Vanity of Dogmatizing Glanvill
epithet: The book behind the Scholar-Gipsy
summary: Glanvill's plea against dogmatism and for open inquiry — including sympathetic notice of witchcraft and the powers of the soul — the book whose wandering scholar Arnold made a legend.

title: An Antidote against Atheism
author: Henry More
query: An Antidote against Atheism Henry More
epithet: Ghosts and witches as proofs of the spirit
summary: More's argument for God and the soul from the evidence of apparitions, witchcraft and providences — the Cambridge Platonist marshalling the uncanny against the materialists.

title: A Treatise concerning Enthusiasme
author: Meric Casaubon
query: A Treatise concerning Enthusiasme Casaubon
epithet: The natural history of religious rapture
summary: Casaubon's analysis of 'enthusiasm' — prophetic rapture, possession and inspiration — as natural states of mind and body; an early psychology of religious and mystical experience.

title: The Certainty of the Worlds of Spirits
author: Richard Baxter
query: The Certainty of the Worlds of Spirits Baxter
epithet: A Puritan divine's evidence for the spirit-world
summary: Baxter's collection of apparitions, witchcrafts and providences gathered to prove the reality of spirits against the growing scepticism — the Puritan companion to Glanvill's Sadducismus.

title: Satan's Invisible World Discovered
author: George Sinclair
query: Satan's Invisible World Discovered Sinclair
epithet: The Scottish casebook of the uncanny
summary: Sinclair's collection of Scottish apparitions, poltergeists and witch-cases — the famous relations of the Devil of Glenluce and Major Weir — a founding book of British ghost-lore.

title: An Historical, Physiological and Theological Treatise of Spirits
author: John Beaumont
query: Historical Treatise of Spirits Beaumont
epithet: A believer's natural history of genii and fairies
summary: Beaumont's treatise on spirits, apparitions, witchcraft and the 'genii' — written by a man who claimed to see them himself, a curious bridge between demonology and the coming age of reason.

title: The Displaying of Supposed Witchcraft
author: John Webster
query: The Displaying of Supposed Witchcraft Webster
epithet: The physician's case against the witch-hunt
summary: Webster's sceptical answer to Glanvill and More, arguing that most 'witchcraft' was fraud, disease or delusion — one of the strongest English arguments against the reality of the witch.

title: The Wars of David and the Peaceable Reign of Solomon
author: Jane Lead
query: The Wars of David Jane Lead
epithet: A Philadelphian allegory of the inner kingdom
summary: Lead's allegorical reading of the reigns of David and Solomon as the soul's warfare and its coming peace — a late visionary work of the Philadelphian prophetess.
